title: Product PRD, Roadmap and Pricing Q1 2026
author: Aisha Kumar
summary: Consolidated product documentation covering the Q1 2026 product goals: product overview, PRD and requirements for the 'Adaptive Routing & Quantization' initiative, high-level design specs, roadmap and themes for the next two quarters, and pricing & packaging notes including release highlights.
body:
Overview

This document consolidates the product overview, PRD, design specs, roadmap themes, pricing guidance, and release notes for Q1 2026 workstreams. It is intended for engineering, product, sales, and customer success stakeholders.

1) Product overview

Goal: Make inference economics predictable for mid-market and enterprise customers while preserving developer ergonomics. Key pillars for this quarter: Adaptive routing, quantization workflows, and improved cost observability for per-route billing.

Scope: Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, Private deployment compatibility; shipping API backwards-compatible changes and a new pricing tier for high-throughput customers.

Success metrics (KPIs):
- Latency P50/P95 targets maintained for top 10% of customers
- 15% reduction in token cost for batch-friendly workloads via quantization and batching improvements
- GA of per-route cost analytics for customers on Dedicated by end of Q1

2) PRD: Adaptive Routing & Quantization (ARQ)

Problem statement:
Many customers run heterogeneous workloads with varying latency/cost requirements. Today routing is static and quantization profiles are manual, causing suboptimal cost and degraded reliability during load spikes.

Primary objectives:
- Automatically route inference requests to the optimal model variant (fp16, int8, or CPU fallback) based on SLOs, cost budget, and availability.
- Provide per-customer quantization profiles and a one-click recommendation flow in the Console.
- Ensure transparent observability showing before/after cost, latency, and quality impact for recommended changes.

Non-goals:
- Replacing model accuracy evaluation pipelines (we will integrate with existing eval-harness).

Requirements (must-have):
1. Runtime: support runtime-side routing policy with policy keys: latency_target_ms, cost_priority (low/medium/high), region_preference.
2. Console: UI to surface recommendations with expected cost delta and estimated quality impact.
3. API: Add optional request-level hints: routing_policy: {"latency_ms":"50","cost_priority":"low"} (backwards compatible).
4. Observability: Per-route cost and token-level breakdown in the Console and via CSV export.
5. Security: All decisions logged and available in audit logs; compatible with Private deployments' KMS controls.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end tests demonstrate routing reduces cost by at least 10% on benchmarked batch workloads without violating configured latency SLOs.
- Console flows reviewed by UX and integrated with rollout A/B controls.
- Documentation and migration guide published.

3) Design specs (high-level)

Architecture overview:
- Policy Engine (control plane) evaluates incoming request metadata and current capacity signals to decide routing.
- Runtime Adapters on serving nodes implement model variant selection and quantization-aware execution paths.
- Telemetry pipeline forwards routing decisions and inference metrics to Console aggregation.

Design constraints and decisions:
- Decision record: ADR-2026-03 - choose adaptive routing as control-plane driven policy to decouple from serving runtime.
- Quantization profiles stored per-customer with semantic versioning to support rollbacks.

Example policy JSON (UI/API contract):
{
  "routing_policy": {
    "latency_target_ms": "50",
    "cost_priority": "low",
    "model_whitelist": ["redwood/gpt-small:1.2", "redwood/gpt-small-quant:1.2-int8"]
  }
}

Operational considerations:
- Fallback policies: if quantized variant increases latency above SLO, runtime must fallback to a compatible fp16 model and record the incident.
- Capacity signals must be propagated within 500ms to Policy Engine for responsive routing.

4) Roadmap and themes (Q1-Q2 2026)

Q1 2026 (current):
- GA: Adaptive Routing & Quantization (ARQ) with per-route cost analytics for Dedicated customers.
- Beta: Console recommendation flow for quantization profiles.
- Research: Kernel-level quantization performance tuning for A100 and H100 fleets.

Q2 2026:
- Expand ARQ to Hosted API customers with opt-in per-tenant policies.
- Launch new pricing tier: High-Throughput Reserved for Dedicated customers (see pricing notes).
- Advance model catalog with Redwood-verified quantized checkpoints.

Milestones and owners:
- Feature spec complete: 2025-12-15 - Owner: Product (Aisha Kumar)
- Engineering design review: 2026-01-10 - Owner: Eng (Runtime)
- Beta release to select customers: 2026-01-31 - Owner: Eng (Platform)
- GA release: 2026-03-25 - Owner: Product + Go-to-market

5) Pricing and packaging notes

New packaging options to support ARQ and high-throughput customers:
- High-Throughput Reserved (Dedicated): monthly commitment with tiered discounts based on committed tokens/second. Includes SLA: 99.9% uptime and priority routing for ARQ.
- Quantization Support Add-on: one-time onboarding fee + per-model verification fee for quantized checkpoints (applies to Dedicated and Private).
- Per-route observability: included in Enterprise tier; add-on for Standard tier.

Example pricing guidance (illustrative):
- Dedicated High-Throughput tier: $X00k/month for 500k tokens/sec reserved, 30% discount on overage tokens.
- Quantization verification: $5k per model checkpoint validated.

Packaging rules:
- Offer free 90-day trial of ARQ recommendation engine for new Dedicated customers.
- Migration discounts: existing Dedicated customers get pro-rated pricing for the first quarter after adoption.

6) Release notes (Q1 2026 GA)

Release: Adaptive Routing & Quantization v1.0 (GA) - 2026-03-25
Highlights:
- Adaptive, policy-driven routing across model variants (fp16, int8, CPU fallback)
- Console: recommendation workflow and per-route cost analytics (CSV export)
- API: optional routing_policy request hint (backwards compatible)
- New Dedicated: High-Throughput Reserved packaging and pricing options

Notable fixes and limitations:
- Initial rollout limited to supported model families; customers using custom models should contact support for quantization verification.
- Observability export formats V1 (CSV) - JSON/Parquet planned for Q2.

Migration and rollout plan:
1. Internal dogfooding (2 weeks) - Eng + Growth teams
2. Invite-only beta (4 weeks) - 10 customers across enterprise and ISV segments
3. Gradual GA with canary ramping (50% -> 100% of Dedicated fleet in 3 weeks)
